companyDescription: Space data & analytics · 100+ nanosatellite constellation for weather (GNSS-RO), maritime/aviation tracking, and RF geolocation · $65M+ in fresh NOAA/EUMETSAT bookings since August · Diehl Defence missile-tracking MOU still the moonshot lever
priceNote: Cached live $9.35 is the Nov 10 regular-session close. After the Q3 miss, shares traded ~$7.92 after hours (-15%), so expect a gap down today. Entry zones are set off the after-hours level.
summary: RESOLVED (Q3, Nov 10) — a revenue miss. Revenue was $18.0M (+42% y/y, +77% ex-maritime) vs ~$20.5M consensus. The FY guide of $75–80M is below the $81.5M Street number and implies a back-end-loaded Q4 of $23–28M. Shares fell ~15% after hours to ~$7.92. The positives are real: non-GAAP gross margin recovered to 49% (from the Q2 34% dip), op cash burn fell to $5.0M, cash is $78M with no debt, and RPO is $175M. But the dated catalyst is gone and the Diehl missile-tracking MOU is undated. Base is cut from +45% to +30% and Moon from +250% to +200%, and the label moves to ค่าขนม. Base bias +72.7pp vs realized 30d P75 +12.2%, so Base is a post-catalyst horizon, not a 30-day call. แนะนำ 1–2% ของ portfolio เท่านั้น — ถ้า thesis fail ลงได้ 35–50%.

catalysts.description: The back-end-loaded Q4 and any conversion of the Diehl missile-tracking MOU into a contract are the next tests; neither is dated.

risks: Gross margin slipped to 34% in Q2 on the WildFireSat contract cancellation; Q3 needs to show recovery.

partnership_win is the measured Tier-2 LAGGARD in turbo feedback (medianExcessVsBenchPct -3.8pp vs +2.0pp overall, n=16; 3/16 windows had SPY down >2%), and it is independently the laggard in the core lane too (-1.6 vs +1.4, n=12). Contract headlines have not reliably converted into sustained re-rates lane-wide.
The Diehl Defence relationship is still a non-binding MOU with no confirmed progress. The moonshot lever is undated.
TTM revenue is down ~33% (post-maritime divestiture), and the business depends on lumpy government renewals and appropriations.
52-week range $6.60-$25.93: this stock has already round-tripped a huge move once this cycle.

macroRisk.rateOutlook: The Fed held at 3.75–4.00% on Oct 28. After the hot Oct CPI on Nov 10, CME FedWatch prices a +25bp hike at the Dec 9 FOMC at ~89–100%, with ~10% odds of 50bp. The 10-year is ~4.98%.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Oct CPI: headline +0.4% m/m, core +0.3% m/m vs 0.2% expected. Sep core PCE 3.1% y/y. Oct PCE (Nov 25) and Nov CPI (Dec 10) are next.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Government-contract space-data company. Rates affect the small-cap multiple more than the business, which depends on appropriations.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — a 25bp December hike is priced after the hot CPI. The tails are a 50bp move or a hot Nov 25 PCE, both of which hit small caps first, so the dip entry is preferred.

catalystSpot.preRunup: Falling, not running: SPIR is ~21% below the Sep 29 report price despite the NOAA award, consistent with the partnership_win lane pattern of contract headlines not sticking.

postWin.note: Redwire (RDW) rallied roughly 220% on Golden Dome missile-defense contract momentum (SHIELD IDIQ award, Feb 2026) — the closest same-theme comparable for what a Diehl Defence contract conversion could do to SPIR. Per this run's tier2 feedback, partnership_win is a lane-wide laggard (-3.8pp vs +2.0pp overall, n=16), so this needs to be a real conversion, not just incremental bookings, to move the needle.

postLose.note: SPIR's own Q2 2026 print is now the most relevant precedent — a genuinely strong bookings quarter ($65M+ in new contracts) still produced a -17.8% stock decline over six weeks on the WildFireSat margin miss, showing this stock can fall hard even on net-positive news.
